title: Find the Minimum and Maximum Number of Nodes Between Critical Points
summary: Define a critical point in a linked list as a node that is either a local maxima or minima.
statement: Define a critical point in a linked list as a node that is either a local maxima or minima. A node is a local maxima if its value is strictly greater than its previous and next nodes. A node is a local minima if its value is strictly less than its previous and next nodes. A node can only be a critical point if it has both a previous and next node. Given a linked list head, return an array of two elements: the minimum and maximum distances between any two distinct critical points. If there are fewer than two critical points, return [-1, -1].
constraints: The linked list has at least two nodes.
A non-endpoint is critical when strictly greater than both neighbors or strictly less than both.
Return [minimum consecutive critical distance,first-to-last distance], or [-1,-1] with fewer than two points.
hints: Criticality depends on a three-node window, and only the positions of critical nodes matter afterward.
Walk with previous,current,next, recording indices where the two differences have the same positive sign.
If fewer than two return [-1,-1]; minimum is adjacent-position gap and maximum is last-first.
Every critical node is detected once; the closest pair in sorted positions is adjacent, while the farthest pair is the endpoints.
editorial: Every critical node is detected once; the closest pair in sorted positions is adjacent, while the farthest pair is the endpoints.

tests.explanation: No node has both neighbors, so there are fewer than two critical points.
Critical indices two, four, and five give minimum distance one and maximum three.
